panels.title: Process
panels.description: Whether Prometheus's last scrape of rsi-train's /metrics endpoint succeeded. 1 = reachable, 0 = the process is down or the metrics server can't be reached.

panels.title: Generation
panels.description: Current Teacher generation number. Increases by one every time a Student beats its Teacher and gets promoted (pkg/lineage).

panels.title: Current round / epoch
panels.description: The round and Student-training epoch currently in progress. Epoch shows -1 between rounds, before the new round's first epoch completes.

panels.title: Epoch / round progress
panels.description: Two bars, both 0-100%, pairing with 'Current round / epoch' to the left: 'epoch progress' is 100 * rsi_epoch_trajectories_started / rsi_epoch_rollout_size (how far the in-progress epoch's rollout collection has gotten toward its trajectory target, resetting to 0 whenever the epoch count advances); 'round progress' is 100 * (rsi_current_epoch + 1) / rsi_epochs_per_generation (how far through the round's own epoch budget that epoch count is, resetting to 0 at the next round's start, when rsi_current_epoch resets to -1).

panels.title: Parallel envs
panels.description: rsi_parallel_envs — the number of parallel bot sessions currently connected. Changeable mid-run via POST /config/parallel-envs?n=N (rsi-train's metrics port), applied at the next round boundary rather than instantly.

panels.title: Rounds won
panels.description: Total completed rounds where the Student beat the Teacher. Honors $lifetime_scope (see its own description): All-time reads rsi_rounds_total's raw value directly, Selected time range uses increase() over $__range. Not $lookback's 30d/$__range duration swap - that one still goes through Prometheus's own stored history for its "all-time" option, which was actively wrong here (found live 2026-10-12: read 0 instead of 1, because the real win happened before a gap in Prometheus's own retained samples). rsi_rounds_total doesn't need that any more: it's restart-surviving at the exporter level now (cmd/rsi-train/roundcounter.go persists it to interimDir/round-counter.json and reloads it on startup).

panels.title: Rounds lost
panels.description: Total completed rounds where the Teacher held. Not wasted work — the Student's updates are simply discarded and the next round tries again from the same Teacher. Honors $lifetime_scope, same reasoning as "Rounds won" next to it - see its own description.

panels.title: Win rate
panels.description: Share of completed rounds the Student has won. Honors $lifetime_scope, same reasoning as "Rounds won"/"Rounds lost" - see their own descriptions.

panels.title: Average return per epoch
panels.description: rsi_epoch_avg_return — the mean total reward per rollout episode in the batch that produced each Student-training epoch. This is the core "is it learning" signal: within a round it should trend up (or at least not collapse) as epochs progress; compare its level across rounds only loosely, since the curriculum's task mix varies episode to episode.

panels.title: Training throughput (samples/sec)
panels.description: rate(rsi_epoch_samples_total[5m]) — how many rollout steps (samples) Student training is consuming per second. A sustained drop usually means the live Minecraft session has slowed down (server load, network), not that PPO itself changed.

panels.title: Teacher vs. Student reward per round
panels.description: rsi_teacher_reward / rsi_student_reward — each side's mean evaluation reward from the most recently completed round. A Student point above its Teacher point at the same round means it won and was promoted (see Generation above).

panels.title: Average round duration
panels.description: Mean wall-clock time per completed round (all epochs of Student training plus both sides' evaluation episodes). Honors $lifetime_scope (see its own description): All-time divides rsi_round_duration_seconds_lifetime_total - a restart-surviving Gauge, since Histograms (rsi_round_duration_seconds itself) have no public API to seed their internal sum/count the way a plain Counter's Add does; see cmd/rsi-train/lifetimemetrics.go - by sum(rsi_rounds_total) (also restart-surviving). Selected time range uses increase() over $__range on both the Histogram's own sum and count, same as before.

panels.title: Task mix
panels.description: How the curriculum's random per-episode task selection has actually split across tasks, over $lifetime_scope (All-time by default - cumulative counts only ever grow; compare shapes, not absolute size). Only present when rsi-train was started with -curriculum-config. See "Task mix balance" below for whether the split is actually even. All-time reads rsi_task_episodes_total's raw per-task values directly - restart-surviving at the exporter level now (cmd/rsi-train/lifetimemetrics.go) - rather than increase() over Prometheus's own possibly-gapped history. Switch $lifetime_scope to "Selected time range" to see task selection over just the dashboard's visible window instead.

panels.title: Student advantage vs. promotion threshold
panels.description: rsi_eval_paired_diff (Student minus Teacher mean evaluation reward, same tasks on each side) against the advantage a Student needs to be promoted: rsi_eval_win_zscore_threshold standard errors (rsi_eval_paired_diff_stderr). The advantage line must sit above the threshold line for a win; when the two policies are equally good it should hover around zero, well below it. Values are the most recently completed round's.

panels.title: Evaluation spread and sample size
panels.description: rsi_eval_reward_std by side (per-episode evaluation reward spread) and rsi_eval_episodes (episodes per side, summed over every environment) for the most recently completed round. A large spread with a small sample is why a single round's teacher/student comparison can't be trusted on its own.

panels.title: Episode outcomes/sec
panels.description: sum(rate(rsi_episodes_total[5m])) by outcome — completed episode success, failure, and truncation rates. A truncation means a new reset began before the prior episode reported Done.

panels.title: Episode starts and steps/sec
panels.description: rates of rsi_episodes_started_total and rsi_episode_steps_total — live environment activity. In curriculum runs, task labels identify the selected goto, mine, or craft episode.

panels.title: Step duration by task (p50/p95/p99)
panels.description: histogram_quantile over rsi_step_duration_seconds by task — per-environment-step wall-clock time (network round-trip plus in-game action wait, e.g. a mine/craft tick). Meant to surface slow steps (a stuck retry loop, a blocking sleep) directly, rather than requiring manual log-timestamp correlation.

panels.title: Gradient updates/sec
panels.description: rate(rsi_gradient_updates_total[5m]) — optimizer update throughput during Student training.

panels.title: Reset failures
panels.description: sum(increase(rsi_reset_failures_total[$__range])) — environment reset failures during the selected dashboard range.

panels.title: Step errors
panels.description: sum(increase(rsi_step_errors_total[$__range])) — environment step failures during the selected dashboard range.

panels.title: Cumulative completion rate
panels.description: Cumulative successful episode completions divided by all cumulative episode attempts (success + failure + truncated). Truncated episodes count against the rate, same as failure, since the task was never actually completed - a truncation just means a new reset began before the prior episode reported Done, rather than the episode reporting Done itself. Success is the reward-based completion proxy used by rsi-train.

panels.title: Completion rate by task
panels.description: Cumulative successful episode completions divided by all cumulative episode attempts (success + failure + truncated) for each selected task type. Truncated episodes count against the rate, same as failure - see 'Cumulative completion rate' panel's description. The task label is assigned when the curriculum poses the episode.

panels.title: Chosen actions by task (share of steps)
panels.description: rsi_actions_total — which action the policy picked, as a share of each task's steps over 10 minutes. Read with the step-duration histogram: for mine_far, most steps finish instantly because the policy picked an action that did nothing (Mine before the block is in view, GoToTarget after arriving, Wait). A policy that has learned the sequence spends its steps on goto until the block appears and then mine.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (task, action) (rate(rsi_actions_total[10m])) / on(task) group_left sum by (task) (rate(rsi_actions_total[10m]))

panels.title: Process CPU usage
panels.description: rate(process_cpu_seconds_total[1m]) — CPU cores in use by the trainer process itself (1.0 = one full core saturated; this process is multi-threaded, so it can exceed 1.0). Exposed automatically by the Prometheus client library, not a custom rsi_* metric. Found live (2026-10): a busy-wait bug and an uncached per-call lookup in mc-agent's pathfinding together held this at 3-4 the whole run; both are fixed as of mc-agent v0.0.36/v0.0.37, after which it should sit low except during real bursts of PPO gradient computation.

panels.title: Process memory usage
panels.description: process_resident_memory_bytes (RSS, the OS-level view) and go_memstats_heap_alloc_bytes (what Go's own heap thinks is live) for the trainer process. RSS normally sits above heap-in-use; a sustained, growing gap between them is itself worth noticing, not just a rising RSS alone.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: go_goroutines — live goroutine count. A steady climb (rather than a bounded, roughly-flat count tracking rsi_parallel_envs) is the signature a prior live incident had: a busy-wait bug left dozens of goroutines stuck runnable, visible here before it was diagnosed via a SIGQUIT stack dump.

panels.title: Task mix balance (% deviation from other tasks' average)
panels.description: For each task, 100 * (its count - the average of every OTHER task's count) / that average - i.e. how far above or below the rest of the curriculum's tasks it currently sits, as a percentage. A perfectly even split sits at 0% for every task; the thresholds flag a task that's meaningfully over- or under-represented relative to the others, not an arbitrary absolute count. ±15% green, ±15-30% orange, beyond ±30% red. Uses barchart rather than bargauge specifically so bars are centered on zero (extending left for a negative deviation, right for a positive one) - bargauge has no such mode, it always fills from its configured min toward the value, which floored every negative bar at the min edge instead of showing it relative to zero. axisSoftMin/Max keep the ±30 threshold band visually legible without clipping anything further out. The organize transform drops Time/instance/job - Prometheus's table format turns every label into its own column, and barchart's auto-detected category axis otherwise grabs whichever string column sorts first (instance), not task. Every rsi_task_episodes_total reference honors $lifetime_scope (see its own description), same as "Task mix" above - All-time reads the raw, now-restart-surviving counter directly, Selected time range uses increase() over $__range. This panel used to wrap every reference in increase(...[$lookback]) instead, a lesser fix from when rsi_task_episodes_total still reset on every restart (found live 2026-10-12, same root cause as "Rounds won"/"Rounds lost").

targets.expr: 100 * (sum by (task) (($lifetime_scope * rsi_task_episodes_total + (1-$lifetime_scope) * increase(rsi_task_episodes_total[$__range]))) - (scalar(sum(($lifetime_scope * rsi_task_episodes_total + (1-$lifetime_scope) * increase(rsi_task_episodes_total[$__range])))) - sum by (task) (($lifetime_scope * rsi_task_episodes_total + (1-$lifetime_scope) * increase(rsi_task_episodes_total[$__range])))) / (scalar(count(sum by (task) (($lifetime_scope * rsi_task_episodes_total + (1-$lifetime_scope) * increase(rsi_task_episodes_total[$__range]))))) - 1)) / ((scalar(sum(($lifetime_scope * rsi_task_episodes_total + (1-$lifetime_scope) * increase(rsi_task_episodes_total[$__range])))) - sum by (task) (($lifetime_scope * rsi_task_episodes_total + (1-$lifetime_scope) * increase(rsi_task_episodes_total[$__range])))) / (scalar(count(sum by (task) (($lifetime_scope * rsi_task_episodes_total + (1-$lifetime_scope) * increase(rsi_task_episodes_total[$__range]))))) - 1))

panels.title: Episode length by outcome (p50/p90/p99, training only)
panels.description: histogram_quantile over rsi_episode_length_steps by task and outcome, scoped to chain_place/chain_use (the only tasks with persistently elevated truncation after the mc-agent client-sync timeout fix - see docs/plans/13) and filtered to phase="training". truncated lands at the active step cap almost by definition; the question this answers is where success/failure fall relative to it: short with a thin tail near the cap means episodes that don't finish are getting stuck early, not merely running a little long - a tail hugging the cap would instead mean some near-misses really would finish with a larger step-len budget. The training filter matters: a round's Teacher/Student evaluation episodes share this metric too, with a 200-step cap (-eval-episode-len) instead of training's 100 - without it, an eval episode's longer length looked like an impossible training outlier (found live 2026-10-03: p99 chain_use/truncated reading 200).

panels.title: Trajectories started this epoch
panels.description: rsi_epoch_trajectories_started vs. its target, rsi_epoch_rollout_size - the raw counts behind the 'Current round / epoch' panel's epoch-progress bar near the top of the dashboard.

panels.title: Which task is active right now (episode starts/min, by task)
panels.description: rate(rsi_task_episodes_total[1m]) by task - updates live during an epoch's ongoing rollout collection (not just at epoch boundaries), so this is the closest thing to 'what is each parallel env working on right now' without per-env task labels. Only emitted when -curriculum-config is set.

panels.title: Average epoch duration
panels.description: Mean wall-clock time per completed Student-training epoch (rsi_epoch_rollout_size trajectories collected plus one PPO update over them). Honors $lifetime_scope, same reasoning as "Average round duration" - see its own description. All-time divides rsi_epoch_duration_seconds_lifetime_total by rsi_epochs_total (both restart-surviving).

panels.title: Episode termination reasons
panels.description: Environment termination reasons and collector-boundary truncations. A collector_truncation means the rollout limit was reached without the environment returning Done=true.

panels.title: Mine action availability
panels.description: Action-mask counts by task, action, and legality. For mine tasks, Mine legal=false means no visible target was available; compare it with Wait legal=true to distinguish a forced wait from a policy choice.

panels.title: PPO losses and entropy
panels.description: Mean policy loss, value loss, and entropy across real replayed rollout steps in the most recently completed epoch. Losses include the configured value coefficient and are averaged over PPO replay passes; entropy is in nats.

panels.title: Raw GAE advantage statistics
panels.description: Raw GAE advantage mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum before PPO batch normalization. Large spread or drifting extrema can explain noisy policy updates.

panels.title: Gradient norms by objective
panels.description: Mean L2 gradient norms per Adam update. Combined before/after-clipping norms show optimizer clipping; policy-plus-entropy versus value norms show whether a shared trunk is dominated by one objective.

list.name: lookback
list.label: Cumulative window
list.description: Not currently used by any panel on this dashboard (2026-10-12) - kept available for any FUTURE "since the start of the run" panel on a metric that doesn't have its own restart-survival fix. Switches such a panel between the true all-time total (30d, comfortably covering this run's history, PROVIDED Prometheus's own retained history actually reaches back that far without a gap) and whatever window the time picker above is set to. Every panel that used to rely on this (Rounds won/lost, Win rate, Average round duration, Average epoch duration, Task mix, Task mix balance) now uses $lifetime_scope instead (see its own description) - each of their underlying metrics is restart-surviving at the exporter level now, so for them, increase() over this window was not just unnecessary but could be actively wrong whenever Prometheus's own retained history had a gap (found live 2026-10-12 - this run's own scrape history was missing several hours around a WSL crash, well within this 30d window, which made increase() undercount).

list.name: lifetime_scope
list.label: Lifetime scope
list.description: Switches Rounds won/Rounds lost/Win rate/Average round duration/Average epoch duration/Task mix/Task mix balance between the true all-time total (1: reads each metric's own raw value directly - correct regardless of Prometheus's own retention/scrape gaps, since the exporter persists and restores all of them itself across restarts; see cmd/rsi-train/roundcounter.go and cmd/rsi-train/lifetimemetrics.go) and however much happened within the time picker's own window above (0: increase() over $__range, which needs Prometheus to have actually scraped that window, same restart-sensitivity as $lookback). Deliberately separate from $lookback - that variable's 30d-vs-$__range duration swap is still the only option for any OTHER metric without its own restart-survival fix, but would make these seven worse: increase() over ANY duration, however long, can still read the wrong answer if the real history it needs has a gap, and 1/0 here is a mask each panel's own formula multiplies by, not a window size.
